cards.explanation: The answer is King David, Israel's king. Jesus asks, "How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?" Everything in this little puzzle hangs on that name, friends. Keep your eye on it, because David is about to speak for himself.

The answer is the Lord Himself. In the psalm the Lord says to the one at His right hand, "…until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet." See the "I"? The Lord is the one doing the making. The one at His right hand gets to sit while the Lord handles it.

The answer is Lord. Jesus says, "Thus David calls Him ‘Lord.’…" Now hold that next to the question of how the Christ can also be David's son, friends. Jesus leaves that question hanging out there for everyone to chew on.

The answer is long robes. Jesus says the scribes "…like to walk around in long robes…" Notice He says they like walking around in them, friends. I think they were doing a lot of strolling. If I had a robe that long, my apron would be jealous.

The answer is False. Jesus says the scribes love "…the places of honor at banquets." He says they love the chief seats in the synagogues too. These folks were aiming for the front, not the back row, friends.

The answer is to put on a show. Jesus says they "…for a show make lengthy prayers." So the length was part of the performance, friends. It sits right alongside defrauding widows of their houses. It's a heavy part of what Jesus says, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "These men will receive greater condemnation." He says it right after naming what they do to widows and how they pray for show. The text says what the outcome is, friends, and it's not a reward.

The answer is True, and this is the part that gets me, friends. Jesus says, "Truly I tell you…" and then, "this poor widow has put in more than all the others." Her gift was two small copper coins. And He says she put in more than the rest.

The answer is that she put in all she had to live on. Jesus says the others gave out of their surplus, "…but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on." Friends, Jesus says what made hers more, and it wasn't the size of the coins. I think about that every time I count my crumbs.

The answer is surplus. Jesus says, "…they all contributed out of their surplus…" That means what they had left over. Then He sets her beside them: she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on. Think of a cookie jar, friends: they gave from the extras, and she gave from the bottom of it.
